specAnchors.text: understand that the growth of the pollen tube followed by fertilisation leads to seed and fruit formation

primer.text: Pollination only parks the pollen; fertilisation finishes the journey. This note follows the pollen tube down the style to the ovary, watches the two nuclei fuse into a zygote, and then tracks the aftermath — the ovule swelling into a seed while the flower around it becomes the fruit that disperses it.

modules.title: Pollen Tube to Zygote
modules.opening: After pollination succeeds, the pollen grain grows a tube down the style toward the ovary; the pollen nucleus travels that tube and fuses with the ovum nucleus, forming the zygote where fertilisation is complete.
keyPoints: Once pollination lands pollen on the stigma, the grain grows a tube that carries its male nucleus toward the ovary.
The tube grows down the style toward the ovary.
The pollen nucleus travels down the pollen tube.
Fertilisation completes when pollen nucleus and ovum nucleus merge into a single zygote.

low.restatement: The pollen drills a tunnel down the style and its nucleus rides it to the egg cell for the fusion.
low.analogy: A miner digging a shaft so the payloader can reach the vault.
low.examPointer: Keep pollination and fertilisation separate — landing versus fusing.

medium.restatement: The tube exists because pollen cannot move itself through tissue; its growth is the delivery system, and only the nucleus makes the trip, meeting the ovum deep in the ovary for the fusion that starts the new plant.
medium.analogy: A train laid to a station so the passenger can board.
medium.examPointer: Name the two nuclei that fuse — pollen nucleus and ovum nucleus — in the definition.

modules.title: Seeds, Fruits and Dispersal
modules.opening: Fertilisation flips the flower's afterlife: each fertilised ovule swells into a seed, and the flower parts around the ovary develop into a fruit that packages those seeds for dispersal — eaten by animals or hitching rides on fur with sticky hooks.
keyPoints: Once fertilisation is done, the ovule swells into a seed.
The flower parts wrapped around that ovule then grow into a fruit.
The fruit contains the seeds and provides a mechanism for seed dispersal.
Some fruits are eaten by animals, which disperse the seeds in their droppings.
Some fruits carry sticky hooks that catch in the fur of passing animals.

low.restatement: Ovule to seed, flower wall to fruit; the fruit then ships the seeds away.
low.analogy: The seed is the parcel, the fruit is the padded envelope, and animals are the postal service.
low.examPointer: Map the transformations — ovule to seed, surroundings to fruit — in that order.

medium.restatement: Dispersal pays because a seed germinating beside its parent competes with it; animal droppings and hooked fur both move seeds far from the parent plant, spreading the next generation into fresh ground.
medium.analogy: Children moving out of the family home rather than crowding one roof.
medium.examPointer: Give one named dispersal mechanism with its fruit adaptation to score fully.

glossary.definition: The tube growing from a pollen grain down the style to deliver the male nucleus.
The fusion of the pollen nucleus with the ovum nucleus to form a zygote.
The ovary structure that develops into a seed after fertilisation.
